title: Random MIME boundary with 8-retry loop — worth defending
description: sign.rs random_boundary() uses 16 random bytes (hex-encoded) to produce a boundary, checking that the boundary string doesn't appear in content, retrying up to 8 times. A hash-derived boundary (previous design) could be predicted by an adversary who controls the content, allowing a crafted message to cause a deterministic signing failure. The random boundary eliminates this attack surface. P(collision across 8 attempts) < 2^-448 for any fixed content. A contributor suggesting 'simplify to SHA-256(content)' should be told the hash-derived design was explicitly replaced for this reason.
close_reason: Random boundary rationale in sign.rs:340 comment: prevents adversarial content from causing deterministic signing failure
